task: I recorded a 3.5-minute Hindi monologue at sample_data/demo2_hindi_spoken_monologue.ogg and need to know exactly what was said. Give me the full Hindi wording as text so I can quote it accurately in an article.
rationale: transcribe_audio is the only tool that returns spoken words as text. Its contract handles files of any duration by slicing them into 30-second-or-less chunks at natural pauses internally, and it converts OGG to PCM16 WAV before calling the ASR model. chunk_audio would only write slice files and return their paths, adding a step while still leaving the user with no transcript.

task: The 3.5-minute recording at sample_data/demo2_hindi_spoken_monologue.ogg is too long for our review meeting. Cut it at natural pauses into clips of about 25 seconds each and give me the list of clip files; I do not need any text from it.
rationale: chunk_audio exists to persist silence-aligned slices and returns chunks_count plus chunk_files, which is exactly the requested deliverable. transcribe_audio also splits long audio, but only inside a temporary directory as an implementation detail: it returns the joined transcript and deletes the slices, so the 25-second clip files would never be handed over.

task: A colleague sent the Tamil clip at sample_data/demo4_tamil_speech_02.webm. I need the spoken words written out in Tamil for the show notes, covering the whole clip from beginning to end.
rationale: transcribe_audio accepts an audio path and returns the transcript; when the clip exceeds the model's 30-second window it splits at silence internally and joins the text, so no manual slicing is required. chunk_audio is a media-slicing helper that makes no speech-to-text call and returns only file paths, so it cannot answer what was said.

task: Our local ASR box only accepts files under 30 seconds. Take sample_data/demo2_hindi_spoken_monologue.ogg, split it at the quietest pauses into pieces shorter than 30 seconds under the run's chunks folder, and report the file paths. Do not send anything to a speech API.
rationale: chunk_audio's contract is to slice audio at silence dips, write the chunks under the active artifacts directory, and return the resulting file paths, exactly the deliverable for an external ASR pipeline. transcribe_audio would consume transcription budget, return merged text, and keep its internal chunks in a temporary directory that is deleted, so the requested files would never exist.

task: Open sample_data/demo6_field_notes.docx and show me only characters 4,000 through 5,999 of the text. I am checking a correction in the middle of the document and do not want the whole file pasted into the chat.
rationale: read_text_file returns a bounded character window plus paging metadata (total_chars, offset, chars_read, has_more), and it extracts .docx content before slicing. extract_document_text also accepts .docx, but it returns the entire document at once and exposes no offset or limit, so it cannot honor the 4,000 to 5,999 character window and would flood the context the user is trying to protect.

task: The two comparison tables in sample_data/demo7_survey_tables.docx have to go into our web CMS as HTML table elements, with every cell and header preserved. Pull them out in that markup.
rationale: extract_document_text's DOCX fast path takes a table_format argument and can emit HTML table markup while preserving cell structure. read_text_file also reads .docx, but it hardcodes Markdown table extraction and exposes no table_format argument, so it cannot produce the requested HTML.

task: Show me the first 1,200 characters of sample_data/demo5_bengali_gitanjali_verses.txt exactly as stored, so I can confirm the Bengali diacritics survived the download unchanged.
rationale: read_text_file reads the UTF-8 bytes directly and returns the exact slice with character counts, so diacritics and dandas are reproduced without interpretation. extract_document_text has no plain-text path: a .txt suffix falls through to the image OCR branch, which would try to OCR the file bytes as a picture, risking a ToolError, hallucinated text, and an unnecessary paid call.

task: I think the download of sample_data/demo5_bengali_gitanjali_verses.txt was cut short. Report its exact total character count and show me the final lines so I can compare them against the source page.
rationale: read_text_file returns total_chars, offset, chars_read, has_more, and next_offset, which lets the caller prove whether the file was truncated and page to the tail. extract_document_text would send the .txt bytes through the image OCR path and return text with no trustworthy character accounting, so it cannot verify truncation and may invent content.

task: The copy of sample_data/demo1_indic_nlp_paper.pdf in our folder is a scanned PDF with no text layer. Pull all of its readable content, including the results tables, into Markdown for our literature review.
rationale: extract_document_text rasterizes every PDF page at 150 DPI and runs Indic-OCR, with table_format controlling how tables are emitted, which is the only way to recover words from a scan with no text layer. inspect_media is explicitly a metadata-only helper: for a PDF it returns page_count and format and makes no OCR call, so it would report the page count but zero content.

task: The image sample_data/demo3_marathi_devanagari_table.png shows a Marathi grammar grid. Rebuild its contents as a Markdown table with the rows and columns intact so I can paste it into our notes.
rationale: extract_document_text sends the PNG through Indic-OCR and can format the recovered table as Markdown while preserving its grid. inspect_media only returns type, file name, size_bytes, and format for an image; it never reads pixel content, so it cannot recover the Marathi cells.

task: Before I upload sample_data/demo3_marathi_devanagari_table.png, tell me its exact size in bytes and its image format. I only need the file facts and do not want any of the text in the picture read.
rationale: inspect_media returns size_bytes and format for an image without any paid model call, exactly the download-completeness check requested. extract_document_text would invoke Indic-OCR and return extracted page text, not the byte size, and would bill an OCR call the user explicitly ruled out.

task: Give me the Tamil equivalent of this English line for a bilingual poster, and put the Tamil wording in the chat with no audio: 'The monsoon arrived early this year and flooded the low-lying fields.'
rationale: translate_text maps text to text and returns the Tamil string directly, matching a chat-only deliverable. synthesize_speech is a text-to-speech tool: it requires Tamil input and writes a WAV, returning a file path and duration rather than the translation, and it cannot perform the English-to-Tamil conversion itself.

task: This Tamil sentence is final approved copy for a radio spot. Record it in a natural female voice as a WAV at artifacts/tamil_narration.wav, keeping the wording exactly as written: 'இந்த ஆண்டு பருவமழை முன்னதாகவே வந்தது; வடிகால் அமைப்புகள் இன்னும் தயாராகவில்லை.'
rationale: synthesize_speech is the only tool that renders text to a WAV file, and output_path lets it write to artifacts/tamil_narration.wav. The source is already Tamil, so translate_text has no language conversion to perform; at best it would echo the same string back as text and produce no audio.

task: We need a Tamil voiceover for this English helpline announcement, saved as artifacts/helpline_ta.wav: 'For assistance, press one. To file a complaint, press two.' The final audio must be in Tamil, not English.
rationale: synthesize_speech does not translate: it speaks the exact text it is given using the voice selected by language, so calling it first would render the English words as English audio even with a Tamil voice setting. The announcement must become Tamil text through translate_text first, and only that Tamil string can be synthesized in the next step.

task: I need the Hindi version of this English notice for a printed handout I am laying out myself. Put the Hindi wording in your reply with no audio and no file: 'The office will remain closed on Friday for maintenance.'
rationale: translate_text maps text to text and returns the Hindi string directly, which is what a printed handout needs. synthesize_speech would produce an audio artifact instead of text and cannot be printed; the explicit no-audio and no-file constraints also rule it out.

task: Save this completed subtitle file exactly as artifacts/episode01_en.srt in UTF-8 so the video editor can load it. Cue 1 runs from 00:00:00,000 to 00:00:04,000 and reads 'Welcome to the show.' Cue 2 runs from 00:00:04,000 to 00:00:09,500 and reads 'Today we are talking about monsoon preparedness.'
rationale: write_text_file writes the supplied string as UTF-8 text and creates parent directories, which is what an .srt deliverable needs. synthesize_speech treats its input as speech and always writes WAV audio; pointing its output_path at episode01_en.srt would leave audio bytes in a file the video editor expects to parse as subtitle text.

task: Record this approved Telugu promo line as audio at artifacts/telugu_promo.wav, using a warm female voice: 'మా కొత్త ఉత్పత్తి ఇప్పుడు అందుబాటులో ఉంది.'
rationale: synthesize_speech generates PCM WAV audio and writes it to output_path, so it can produce a valid .wav from the approved Telugu line. write_text_file only writes UTF-8 characters and cannot encode audio samples, so it would create a corrupt file with a .wav extension.

task: The approved Marathi wording for the website is below. Save it verbatim as UTF-8 Markdown at artifacts/marathi_notice.md with no audio: 'कार्यालय शुक्रवारी देखभालीमुळे बंद राहील.'
rationale: The Marathi text is already final and the task is storage rather than generation, so write_text_file saves it verbatim as UTF-8 Markdown. synthesize_speech would interpret the paragraph as something to speak and write WAV bytes to marathi_notice.md, producing an audio file with a Markdown extension instead of the requested text.
